findings.issue: The four channel cards are held at a fixed width (--channel-card-width: 15.3125rem, copied from the competitor), so the row is centred and takes up only about the middle 70% of the content width. It doesn't start under the left-aligned 'Contact details' heading, and the Hours card breaks its time after the hyphen ('9:00-' / '18:00 China Standard Time').
findings.reference: The competitor's four cards fill the width of their own content column, level with the form and photo above them. Only their style is to be followed (1px #979797 border, radius 10px, icon, black label bar, centred text), not their pixel width.
findings.fix: In reference.css remove --channel-card-width so the cards share the content width and the row starts on the content's left edge under the heading. Keep '9:00–18:00' on one line (white-space: nowrap on the time, or a non-breaking dash in the copy).

findings.issue: The 'Contact details' heading sits right on the first card's top border with almost no gap. At desktop the gap is only a few pixels. Every other section on the page leaves clear space between its heading and its content.
findings.reference: The competitor's card row is set well apart from the content above it, and its headings ('Have Questions?', 'Email Us') have clear space under them.
findings.fix: In reference.css give the channels heading the same space below it as the other sections (e.g. margin-block-end on .block--contactChannels .block__heading, or a row-gap between the heading and .contact-channels).

findings.issue: The five steps show as a plain numbered browser list. The step titles ('Send your files', 'We check feasibility') have the same weight and size as their descriptions, the text is smaller than the intro's body copy, and the lead ('How a free quote moves…') looks like a loose body line. Nothing marks this as a process module.
findings.reference: The competitor's process list (solution page, process:list) is a left heading and text with numbered steps on the right: large blue numerals 01–03, a bold title per step, then text.
findings.fix: Set components.pageTypes.contact.process to "list" in template-variants.json so the steps get numbered markers and bold step titles at body size.

findings.issue: The steps are unstyled here too (plain '1.'–'5.' with titles at body weight). There is also a gap of about 60 px with nothing in it between the lead line and the first step.
findings.reference: The competitor's numbered steps stack straight under their heading and text, each with a numeral and a bold title.
findings.fix: This is fixed by the same process variant ('list'). Then check that the gap between the lead and the steps matches the other sections' heading-to-content gap.

findings.issue: The list item titles ('Contact channels', 'Dedicated specialist', …) are set in regular (400) weight at about 26 px. That is almost the size of the section's 700-weight H2 just above them, so the levels blur and the list reads like a run of headings. The light-teal check marks are also so faint they nearly disappear on the tint.
findings.reference: The competitor sets each level smaller than the one above and its item titles bold (card titles Maison 700 22px under 52–60px h2s). Its check lists use clearly visible markers.
findings.fix: Set components.pageTypes.contact.iconList to "checks", or in reference.css give .block--iconList item titles font-weight 700 and the subheading scale under the h2. Give the check icon a darker colour (e.g. var(--surface-dark) or the link blue).

findings.issue: At desktop too, the item titles are a light 400 weight at a size close to the body lead, with a pale check icon. Next to the bold 700 H2 they look unfinished.
findings.reference: The competitor's item titles are bold (Maison 700) and its markers are clearly visible.
findings.fix: Same change as on mobile: the 'checks' variant, or font-weight 700 on the item titles and a darker check colour.

findings.issue: The consent checkbox is a tiny, pale square of about 12 px, barely visible on the tint and well below a comfortable tap size. It is the one required tick in the form.
findings.reference: The competitor's form fields all have clear 1px black outlines and full-size tap targets.
findings.fix: In reference.css give the form's checkbox a visible 1px black border (or accent-color: #262626) and a size of about 20–24 px, with the label wrapping beside it.

findings.issue: 'SEND ENQUIRY' is a small dark button at the left of the form column. The comment in reference.css calls for a full-width dark SEND bar, but the rule never sets the width.
findings.reference: The competitor's submit is a full-width dark bar (#262626) across the form column.
findings.fix: Add width: 100% (or justify-self: stretch) to the :is(.form-block__form, .cta__form) .button--primary rule in reference.css.

findings.issue: The consent line ends 'as described in the privacy policy. Privacy policy': the words 'privacy policy' appear twice because the copy repeats the link label that follows it.
findings.reference: The competitor's form has no repeated text.
findings.fix: Shorten the consent copy to end before the link (e.g. 'I agree that my details are used to answer this enquiry, as described in our') or make 'privacy policy' in the sentence itself the link.

findings.issue: In the footer's brand column, the STRANDMILL wordmark sits on the left edge while the contact lines and links beneath it are centred, so the column has two alignments.
findings.reference: The competitor's brand column is centred throughout: monogram, STAY CONNECTED, the social icons and the links.
findings.fix: In template.css let .site-footer__brand follow the column (justify-self/text-align: var(--footer-brand-align, start)) instead of a fixed justify-self: start. This site already sets --footer-brand-align: center.

findings.issue: On phones the STRANDMILL wordmark is also left-aligned above a centred block of contact lines and links.
findings.reference: On phones the competitor centres everything in the footer.
